svg.title: Six words, explained with an office
svg.desc: Six cartoon office scenes. Repository is a project binder with an elephant that says "I remember every version": a folder that never forgets. Commit is a camera and a corkboard of dated snapshots, each with a short note: Ctrl+S saves, commit remembers. Branch is a copy of the original: the original, labelled main, sits safely under a glass dome while you scribble on your own copy. Merge is a cheerful glue stick that sticks your branch's changes into main, automatically, mostly. Push and pull are an out-tray sending papers up to the GitHub cloud and an in-tray receiving papers from it; Sync Changes empties both trays. Pull request is you handing a document to a colleague and asking "Can you check this before it goes in?"; the colleague marks a typo on line 3 and presses Approve. Bottom strip: a task in six words, repository, branch, commit, push, pull request, merge, then again.
svg.text: Six words, explained with an office
The jargon is new. The ideas are things you already do at work.

g.text: = a project folder with a memory
A saved moment, with a note
A copy of main for your task.
Git does it for you, automatically.
It only asks for help on a clash.
Comments land on the exact line.
